objective: Proof and computation. In a planar knot space: does a removed line meeting the closing line leave at most four port patterns; with six patterns, does the removed line's hub always reach the ports (tied to one, or in a near knot with two); does that route generate every pinned-and-separated knot; and why do four-pattern interfaces never create? Prove what can be proved, test the rest on generated planar spaces, and state any remaining step as an explicit open problem.
status: Proved by HANDLE-EMERGENCE-20261102-001C-P001: the odd-point model (solutions up to complement = one incidence per line with cycle-sign parities); the skip model on plane knot spaces with Kasteleyn signs (failure by counting: n lines cannot oddly cover n + 2 faces; after a removal the solutions are perfect matchings of the other lines to the faces off the removed line); interfaces (a line meeting the removed line shares a face with it, so at most four patterns); a handle leaves slack (genus g: n + 2 - 2g faces; Fano on the torus: 14 face-odd assignments, 5 solutions by the homology parities); open: planar non-creation
title: Why a planar side cannot create
